note: The build roadmap as machine data (Y-019), GENERATED from docs/YGGDRASIL_BUILD_ROADMAP_2026-10-30.md by yggdrasil.campaign.build_campaign and drift-checked against it by verify_campaign: the markdown is the law, this file is its mirror. Slice text is the roadmap's own wording, reflowed where the markdown wraps a line. Banking state is NOT kept here — it lives in CAMPAIGN_STATE.md.

parts.goal: turn a specification into a buildable project. Every open choice the spec leaves becomes a written decision; every component gets a contract before it gets code.
parts.name: Roots: decisions, contracts, scaffolding

parts.goal: one agent that runs on the Pi, the laptop, and anything between — censusing what it truly has, hosting models through the engines that exist, and minding its own resources like a good neighbour.
parts.name: The Node Agent: every device a citizen

parts.goal: the squirrel that never stops running — discovery, registry, heartbeats, and task/result flow between nodes, secure by default, honest under partition.
parts.name: Ratatoskr: the message fabric

parts.goal: the present-tense Norn. Given a task, choose where it runs — by capability, by load, by measured fitness — and own its whole lifecycle from the spec §4.1 state machine.
parts.name: Verðandi: scheduler & semantic router

parts.goal: the past-tense Norn. The mesh remembers — decisions, contexts, outcomes — as a versioned knowledge graph any node can ask, so the whole tree is wiser than any branch.
parts.name: Urðr: memory & the knowledge graph

parts.goal: the future-tense Norn. Verify what the mesh produces, project what it is about to do, and price risk before it is paid — the spec's most original organ, built with the most honesty about its limits.
parts.name: Skuld: verifier & temporal projection

parts.goal: the mesh's reason to exist — tasks no single small model on a single small device could serve, answered by the tree together: ensembles, role crews, learned routing, and overload grace.
parts.name: Ensembles: many models, one answer

parts.goal: the mesh leaves the bench. Each world-role proven on the class of device it names — or honestly marked NOT PROVEN where the hardware isn't in the house.
parts.name: The Nine Worlds on Real Hardware

parts.goal: the tree serves the house that grew it. Each consumer binds by contract, and each binding is proven by that consumer doing real work through the mesh instead of around it.
parts.name: The Workshop Weave

parts.goal: the addendum's planetary vision, worked as honest research. Most slices here end in findings, prototypes, or NOT PROVEN verdicts — that is their success shape, named in advance.
parts.name: WorldNet Horizon

parts.goal: close the way this house closes — with evidence. The tree's claims, all of them, cashed or corrected in one final accounting.
parts.name: The Proof Spine

slices.text: Spec reconciliation: the v3.1 README + WorldNet addendum read whole; a concordance maps every spec section to the part of this road that builds it (or names it deferred, with the reason).
slices.title: Spec reconciliation

slices.text: ADR-001 Language: Python control plane first (Decision 2), with the compiled-path criteria recorded (measured thresholds that would justify a Mojo/Rust component).
slices.title: ADR-001 Language

slices.text: ADR-002 Transport: the fabric benchmark design (MQTT vs NATS vs minimal gossip on Pi-class hardware, the mesh's real message shapes) — the benchmark itself runs in Part III; the *criteria* are fixed here.
slices.title: ADR-002 Transport

slices.text: ADR-003 State: CRDT scope per Decision 4 — which stores are CRDT-replicated, which are single-writer logs, and the merge rules.
slices.title: ADR-003 State

slices.text: ADR-004 Inference engines: the node wraps Aesir, Ollama, llama.cpp, and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints behind one contract; engine capability reporting is honest and per-engine.
slices.title: ADR-004 Inference engines

slices.text: The node contract v1: identity, capability census, model lifecycle, task execution, health — the interface every engine adapter and every Norn speaks; written before code.
slices.title: The node contract v1

slices.text: The task contract v1: task envelope (id, kind, payload, criticality, context refs, verification needs), result envelope, streaming shape, error taxonomy.
slices.title: The task contract v1

slices.text: The registry contract: model entries (name, sizes/quants, capabilities, device classes, measured speeds) — the spec §4.2 shape, as data schemas.
slices.title: The registry contract

slices.text: Repo scaffolding: package layout, pyproject, test harness, lint, the house no-Docker native-service pattern (systemd units as data), CI as manual-dispatch only (Volmarr's standing default).
slices.title: Repo scaffolding

slices.text: Threat model: node impersonation, poisoned results, gossip spam, malicious tasks — the mesh's enemies named before its doors are built.
slices.title: Threat model

slices.text: Identity foundation: per-node keypairs, node certificates issued by the mesh's own root (the WorldNet §3 seed, local scale), keys kept via Kista where a node supports it.
slices.title: Identity foundation

slices.text: The nine-worlds role model as data: role definitions (capabilities expected, criticality ceilings) assignable per node, changeable by the operator — roles are hats, not hardware.
slices.title: The nine-worlds role model as data

slices.text: Observability contract: what every component logs and meters (structured, local, no phone-home), the Verdandi event shapes reused where they fit.
slices.title: Observability contract

slices.text: The simulator: a loopback multi-node simulator (many fake nodes on one machine) — the road's wind tunnel; every later part tests in it before touching hardware.
slices.title: The simulator

slices.text: Fake engines: deterministic stub inference engines (echo, latency-shaped, failure-shaped) so routing can be proven without models.
slices.title: Fake engines

slices.text: Data discipline: all registries, profiles, and policies are versioned data files with schemas and validators.
slices.title: Data discipline

slices.text: The operator's door (Midgard v0): a CLI that can list nodes, tasks, and health from day one — humans are never locked out of their own tree.
slices.title: The operator's door (Midgard v0)

slices.text: Licence & provenance check: the repo's licence read and honoured; third-party pieces noticed; nothing vendored silently.
slices.title: Licence & provenance check

slices.text: The campaign file: this roadmap as machine data (the Mythic Coder M-201 pattern) so keepers and boards can run it.
slices.title: The campaign file

slices.text: Part I gate: contracts + ADRs + simulator skeleton merged; the concordance published in-repo; zero inference code yet — the roots hold before the trunk rises.
slices.title: Part I gate

slices.text: Node agent skeleton: identity (Y-011), config, lifecycle (start, join, drain, stop), native systemd service.
slices.title: Node agent skeleton

slices.text: Capability census: CPU, RAM, accelerators (CUDA, Hailo, NPU, none), disk, thermals — measured, not assumed; refreshed on change.
slices.title: Capability census

slices.text: Engine adapter I — Ollama: discovery, model list, generate (streaming), honest capability mapping into the node contract.
slices.title: Engine adapter I — Ollama

slices.text: Engine adapter II — Aesir: Aesir's API as it stands; its capability ledger (what is PROVEN on that device) feeds the census — the mesh never promises what Aesir itself marks partial.
slices.title: Engine adapter II — Aesir

slices.text: Engine adapter III — llama.cpp server + generic OpenAI-compatible local endpoints.
slices.title: Engine adapter III

slices.text: Model store: on-node model files with hashes; a model is "present" only when its hash verifies (the Aesir wave discipline).
slices.title: Model store

slices.text: Model lifecycle: load/unload into slots by VRAM/RAM budget; swap costs measured and reported to Verðandi as facts.
slices.title: Model lifecycle

slices.text: The resource governor: per-node ceilings (memory, thermal, CPU share) with graceful refusal — a node sheds load before it cooks (the accelerator-first law's politeness, as code).
slices.title: The resource governor

slices.text: Task execution sandbox: tasks run bounded (time, tokens, output), cancellable, with streamed partial results.
slices.title: Task execution sandbox

slices.text: Node health endpoint: liveness, load, models, governor state — the shape Part III's heartbeats carry.
slices.title: Node health endpoint

slices.text: Local queue: tasks held per node with priorities; a busy node says how busy, in numbers.
slices.title: Local queue

slices.text: Failure shapes: engine crash, OOM, thermal throttle, model corrupt — each detected, contained, and reported distinctly.
slices.title: Failure shapes

slices.text: The Pi citizen: the full agent on Mimir-class ARM, coexisting with Samtal and the Hailo road (the kiosk/Aesir coexistence rules honoured).
slices.title: The Pi citizen

slices.text: The laptop citizen: purplelongship-class x86 + CUDA census, Aesir GPU line as its engine.
slices.title: The laptop citizen

slices.text: The VM citizen: this VM as a CPU-only node — honest speeds, no pretence.
slices.title: The VM citizen

slices.text: Phone-class profile: the agent's shape on a phone (small models, battery governor) — built and simulated; on-device proof recorded as NOT PROVEN until a phone runs it.
slices.title: Phone-class profile

slices.text: Model fetch duty: a node can fetch a model it lacks from a mesh peer or a named source, hash-verified, when policy allows — the mesh carries its own supplies.
slices.title: Model fetch duty

slices.text: Quantisation fitness: per device class, which quants of a model are runnable (registry data from Y-008) enforced at placement time, not discovered at crash time.
slices.title: Quantisation fitness

slices.text: Node journal: every task the node ran with engine, model, timings, outcome — the raw material Urðr ancestry is built from.
slices.title: Node journal

slices.text: Graceful degradation: a node losing its accelerator keeps serving on CPU at declared reduced capability — census updates, no silent lies.
slices.title: Graceful degradation

slices.text: Idle generosity: an idle node advertises spare capacity; a busy one withdraws it — the present-tense truth Verðandi routes on.
slices.title: Idle generosity

slices.text: Node operator tools: drain, pause, inspect, and retire a node from the CLI (Y-017 grown).
slices.title: Node operator tools

slices.text: Security of the agent: tasks are data, never code, unless a signed task kind explicitly says so (threat model Y-010 enforced).
slices.title: Security of the agent

slices.text: Power and thermal telemetry on Pi + laptop; the governor's decisions cite them.
slices.title: Power and thermal telemetry on Pi + laptop

slices.text: Multi-engine node: one node hosting Aesir and Ollama side by side, slots accounted across engines.
slices.title: Multi-engine node

slices.text: Node conformance kit: a test pack any new engine adapter must pass to join (contract, streaming, errors, census honesty).
slices.title: Node conformance kit

slices.text: Soak: one node, 1,000 tasks, mixed engines — leak and drift check with numbers.
slices.title: Soak

slices.text: Part II gate: three real citizens (Pi, laptop, VM) run the conformance kit green against their real engines.
slices.title: Part II gate

slices.text: The transport benchmark (ADR-002 executed): MQTT vs NATS vs minimal gossip on Pi-class + LAN shapes; latency, chatter, memory — the record decides.
slices.title: The transport benchmark (ADR-002 executed)

slices.text: Fabric core: publish/subscribe + direct node channels over the chosen transport, one API for all components.
slices.title: Fabric core

slices.text: TLS everywhere: node certificates (Y-011) on every channel; no plaintext mode exists to accidentally use.
slices.title: TLS everywhere

slices.text: Discovery: nodes find each other on a LAN (mDNS + a seed list) without any cloud rendezvous.
slices.title: Discovery

slices.text: The registry service: nodes register census + models; the registry is itself replicated (no single registrar to kill).
slices.title: The registry service

slices.text: Heartbeats and liveness: missed beats age a node from present → suspect → gone, with the timings as data.
slices.title: Heartbeats and liveness

slices.text: Gossip of state: registry and health propagate epidemically; convergence time measured in the simulator at 3, 10, and 30 nodes.
slices.title: Gossip of state

slices.text: CRDT stores land (ADR-003): registry + membership as CRDTs; merge correctness property-tested.
slices.title: CRDT stores land (ADR-003)

slices.text: Task channel: task offers, claims, and result streams ride the fabric with the Y-007 envelopes; backpressure is explicit.
slices.title: Task channel

slices.text: Partition behaviour: a split mesh keeps working in halves; on healing, CRDTs merge and duplicate task executions are reconciled by task id (never silently double-answered).
slices.title: Partition behaviour

slices.text: Message provenance: every message signed by its node; unsigned or wrongly-signed traffic is dropped and counted.
slices.title: Message provenance

slices.text: Rate and size discipline: per-node quotas on gossip and tasks; a flooding node is throttled by its peers (Níðhöggr's first small tooth, local scale).
slices.title: Rate and size discipline

slices.text: Store-and-forward: a task for a sleeping node waits in the fabric with a TTL; expiry is an event, not a silence.
slices.title: Store-and-forward

slices.text: The fabric on the real LAN: Pi + laptop + VM over the home network, TLS on, discovery unaided.
slices.title: The fabric on the real LAN

slices.text: WAN-shaped simulation: latency/loss profiles in the simulator (the road to WorldNet is tested as shapes, not hopes).
slices.title: WAN-shaped simulation

slices.text: Fabric observability: message rates, convergence, drops — on the operator's door.
slices.title: Fabric observability

slices.text: Versioned protocol: fabric messages carry versions; mixed- version meshes degrade by contract, not by crash.
slices.title: Versioned protocol

slices.text: Restart resilience: a node rejoins and re-syncs its CRDT state without a full reload.
slices.title: Restart resilience

slices.text: The registrar's death drill: kill the first node ever started; the mesh notices nothing but a missing heartbeat.
slices.title: The registrar's death drill

slices.text: Clock discipline: nodes report clock skew; temporal logic (Part VI) never trusts a single node's clock.
slices.title: Clock discipline

slices.text: Fabric conformance kit: any future transport swap must pass the same suite (Decision 3's promise kept).
slices.title: Fabric conformance kit

slices.text: Encrypted payloads for sensitive task kinds: content sealed to the executing node where the task's policy demands.
slices.title: Encrypted payloads for sensitive task kinds

slices.text: Audit tap: an operator-consented, read-only feed of fabric events for debugging — off by default, loud when on.
slices.title: Audit tap

slices.text: Load shapes: heartbeat/gossip overhead measured per node count; the mesh's own cost is a published number.
slices.title: Load shapes

slices.text: Failure drills: node kill mid-task, partition mid-stream, corrupt message injection — recovery proven per drill.
slices.title: Failure drills

slices.text: Part III gate: the three real citizens + 10 simulated nodes hold one registry truth through kills and a partition, evidence banked.
slices.title: Part III gate

slices.text: Task lifecycle state machine (spec §4.1) implemented as the single source of truth for task state; every transition journaled.
slices.title: Task lifecycle state machine (spec §4.1) implemented as the single source of truth for task state

slices.text: Capability matching: task requirements (model, context, vision, tools, quant floor) matched against registry truth — a task is never dealt to a node that cannot truly run it.
slices.title: Capability matching

slices.text: Load-aware placement: current queue depth, slot pressure, and governor state weigh the choice; the reasoning is recorded per decision (why this node — in plain data).
slices.title: Load-aware placement

slices.text: Fitness memory (Urðr's first gift): measured per (node, model, task-kind) speeds and success rates feed placement — yesterday's runs steer today's.
slices.title: Fitness memory (Urðr's first gift)

slices.text: Semantic routing: task kind classification (code, chat, vision, embedding, reasoning…) routes to models registered for that kind; unknown kinds fall back by declared rules.
slices.title: Semantic routing

slices.text: Criticality classes: a critical task buys the most reliable node + verification (Part VI); a casual one buys the cheapest adequate — criticality is in the envelope (Y-007), set by callers.
slices.title: Criticality classes

slices.text: Deadline-aware scheduling: tasks with deadlines are placed by predicted completion (fitness × queue), and a deadline that cannot be met is refused early, honestly.
slices.title: Deadline-aware scheduling

slices.text: Streaming placement: long generations pin to their node; mid-stream node death hands the partial + state to Skuld's rules (Part VI) for resume-or-restart judgement.
slices.title: Streaming placement

slices.text: Batch and fan-out: a task that splits (embed a corpus, map a repo) fans out across nodes and gathers — scatter/gather as a first-class lifecycle.
slices.title: Batch and fan-out

slices.text: Priority and fairness: per-caller shares so one greedy caller can't starve the mesh; the operator's own work preempts by his standing priority.
slices.title: Priority and fairness

slices.text: Placement dry-run: "where would this go and why" as an API — the router explains itself before it acts.
slices.title: Placement dry-run

slices.text: Locality preference: prefer the caller's own device, then the LAN, then further — data rarely travels farther than it must.
slices.title: Locality preference

slices.text: Model-warmth awareness: a node with the model already loaded beats a faster node that must swap (swap costs from Y-027 are in the math).
slices.title: Model-warmth awareness

slices.text: Router as a service any node can host: Verðandi is a role (Y-012), not a machine; its state replicates over the fabric.
slices.title: Router as a service any node can host

slices.text: Router failover: the role moves when its host dies, mid- queue, with the lifecycle journal as the handover.
slices.title: Router failover

slices.text: Anti-flapping: placement hysteresis so borderline tasks don't bounce between nodes.
slices.title: Anti-flapping

slices.text: The Muspelheim trigger (routing half): when the mesh saturates, Verðandi sheds by criticality — casual work waits or refuses; critical work is defended.
slices.title: The Muspelheim trigger (routing half)

slices.text: Caller SDK (Python): submit, stream, cancel, await — the small API every consumer in Part IX uses.
slices.title: Caller SDK (Python)

slices.text: CLI door grows: submit a task from the command line, watch it route, read why.
slices.title: CLI door grows

slices.text: Routing benchmarks: placement quality vs naive round-robin and vs single-best-node on scripted workloads — numbers, not claims.
slices.title: Routing benchmarks

slices.text: Simulator league: routing policies compete in the wind tunnel across load shapes; the league table is data for Part VII.
slices.title: Simulator league

slices.text: Policy as data: placement weights, preferences, and criticality rules are operator-editable data with validators.
slices.title: Policy as data

slices.text: Multi-tenant honesty: two households' meshes never mix — mesh identity is cryptographic (Y-011), not a config string.
slices.title: Multi-tenant honesty

slices.text: Task provenance chain: every result carries (task id, node, engine, model, quant, timings) — the receipt Part VI verifies.
slices.title: Task provenance chain

slices.text: Cancellation done right: a cancelled task stops everywhere, frees its slot, and the cancellation is a journal fact.
slices.title: Cancellation done right

slices.text: Part IV gate: a scripted mixed workload (chat + code + embeddings + one critical) routes across the three real citizens with placement reasons recorded; benchmark vs round-robin banked.
slices.title: Part IV gate

slices.text: Urðr store design: entities (nodes, models, tasks, decisions, contexts, outcomes) and relations, versioned; the schema is data (Y-016).
slices.title: Urðr store design

slices.text: Decision ancestry: every routing decision (Y-077) lands in Urðr with its reasons — "why did this run there" is answerable forever.
slices.title: Decision ancestry

slices.text: Outcome ledger: task outcomes (success, quality signals, failures) join the graph — the fitness memory (Y-078) is a view over this, not a separate pile.
slices.title: Outcome ledger

slices.text: Context service: conversation/project contexts stored as versioned objects; a task references context by id + version, never by copying megabytes around.
slices.title: Context service

slices.text: Context injection: Verðandi attaches the right context slice to a task (by reference resolution at the executing node).
slices.title: Context injection

slices.text: Shared knowledge bases: curated corpora (a project's docs, a household's notes) as Urðr collections with owners and scopes.
slices.title: Shared knowledge bases

slices.text: Retrieval over the graph: structured queries + embedding search (embeddings computed by mesh tasks themselves — the tree feeds its own memory).
slices.title: Retrieval over the graph

slices.text: Replication: Urðr replicates by scope — household graph everywhere, private scopes only where their owner allows.
slices.title: Replication

slices.text: Versioning and time travel: any graph state as of a moment can be read (the past is a place you can visit, carefully).
slices.title: Versioning and time travel

slices.text: Provenance law: every fact in Urðr carries its source (which node, which task, when); unsourced assertions cannot enter.
slices.title: Provenance law

slices.text: Forgetting: facts decay or are deleted on policy/owner word; deletion propagates through replicas and is itself a fact.
slices.title: Forgetting

slices.text: Contradiction handling: conflicting facts coexist with their sources; consumers choose by trust policy — Urðr never silently picks a winner.
slices.title: Contradiction handling

slices.text: The persona seed (WorldNet §6, local scale): a character's canon (prompts, habits, voice notes — the Kista expansion's kin) can live in Urðr as a versioned context any node can embody.
slices.title: The persona seed (WorldNet §6, local scale)

slices.text: Session memory for chat consumers: Samtal/Rúnmál-shaped conversation memory as a standard Urðr pattern (Part IX consumes).
slices.title: Session memory for chat consumers

slices.text: Graph size discipline: compaction, summarisation tasks (run on the mesh), and cold storage to Niflheim-role nodes.
slices.title: Graph size discipline

slices.text: Backup and export: the whole graph as portable files — the household's memory is ownable, like everything else here.
slices.title: Backup and export

slices.text: Privacy scopes enforced at read: a task sees only the scopes its caller holds; scope checks are in the store, not in callers' good intentions.
slices.title: Privacy scopes enforced at read

slices.text: Urðr query door: the CLI/API can ask the graph plainly (decisions for a task, a node's history, a model's record).
slices.title: Urðr query door

slices.text: Cold start: a new node syncs the graph slices it needs and no more; sync cost measured by graph size.
slices.title: Cold start

slices.text: Consistency drills: kill an Urðr host mid-write; replicas converge; no fact is half-born.
slices.title: Consistency drills

slices.text: Quality signals intake: consumer feedback (accepted, corrected, rejected answers) lands as outcome facts for Part VII.
slices.title: Quality signals intake

slices.text: Part V gate: a week-in-a-day simulation — decisions, outcomes, contexts accumulate; ancestry questions answered from the graph alone; forgetting drill passes.
slices.title: Part V gate

slices.text: Verification contracts: per task kind, what "checked" means (schema, invariants, cross-check, second-model review) — as data.
slices.title: Verification contracts

slices.text: Invariant checker service: results validated against declared invariants before delivery; violations quarantined, never silently passed.
slices.title: Invariant checker service

slices.text: Shadow verification: critical tasks (Y-080) are duplicated to a second node/model; agreement is evidence, disagreement is an event with both answers preserved.
slices.title: Shadow verification

slices.text: The Auditor pattern: Nidavellir-role nodes run review tasks (code review, fact check) as ordinary mesh citizens — the workshop's Auditor office, mechanised.
slices.title: The Auditor pattern

slices.text: Temporal projection v1: from Urðr's fitness history + current load, predict a task's completion time and failure risk — with the prediction's own past accuracy tracked.
slices.title: Temporal projection v1

slices.text: Cascade risk: a task whose failure would strand dependents (fan-out parents, campaign slices) is scored; high cascade risk buys verification and checkpointing.
slices.title: Cascade risk

slices.text: Breakage prediction for nodes: thermal trends, error rates, disk pressure → a node's near-future reliability score feeds Verðandi (the future steering the present, as designed).
slices.title: Breakage prediction for nodes

slices.text: Calibration court: Skuld's predictions are graded against outcomes monthly-in-simulation; a miscalibrated predictor is retrained or demoted to advisory — honesty enforced on the prophet herself.
slices.title: Calibration court

slices.text: Canary tasks: synthetic probe tasks continuously measure nodes/models (the mesh takes its own pulse); canary results are Urðr facts.
slices.title: Canary tasks

slices.text: Anomaly flags: a node suddenly slow, a model suddenly wrong-shaped — flagged with evidence, quarantined by policy if severe.
slices.title: Anomaly flags

slices.text: Result attestation: verified results carry Skuld's mark (what was checked, how, outcome) — consumers can demand the mark.
slices.title: Result attestation

slices.text: Temporal debt: tasks deferred by Muspelheim shedding are remembered with their age; the mesh knows what it owes.
slices.title: Temporal debt

slices.text: What-if door: "if I add this workload, what breaks" — projection over the simulator seeded from live Urðr state.
slices.title: What-if door

slices.text: Verification budgets: checking costs mesh capacity; Skuld spends it by criticality and says what it skipped and why.
slices.title: Verification budgets

slices.text: Disagreement tribunal: shadow-verification conflicts are resolved by declared rules (third node, stronger model, human) — never by coin flip, never silently.
slices.title: Disagreement tribunal

slices.text: Projection honesty in the API: every prediction ships with its confidence and its track record; a young Skuld says "I don't know yet" in so many words.
slices.title: Projection honesty in the API

slices.text: Security verification: tasks claiming sensitive kinds get their provenance chain (Y-098) checked link by link.
slices.title: Security verification

slices.text: Long-task checkpoints: streaming tasks checkpoint partial state into Urðr so a node death loses seconds, not the whole task.
slices.title: Long-task checkpoints

slices.text: The Norns together: a single decision trace showing past (Urðr facts), present (Verðandi state), future (Skuld scores) for one task — the trinity made visible, the project's signature demo.
slices.title: The Norns together

slices.text: Failure-injection league: Skuld graded on catching planted faults (wrong results, slow nodes, lying engines) in the simulator.
slices.title: Failure-injection league

slices.text: Advisory mode: Skuld can run observe-only on a young mesh, learning calibration before it is trusted with gates.
slices.title: Advisory mode

slices.text: Part VI gate: the fault-injection league passed at a stated catch rate; calibration report published; the Y-141 trace demonstrated on the real three-node mesh.
slices.title: Part VI gate

slices.text: Ensemble patterns as data: parallel-vote, draft-and-review, decompose-and-delegate, cascade (small first, escalate on doubt) — patterns are named, reusable task shapes.
slices.title: Ensemble patterns as data

slices.text: The cascade: a small local model attempts; its confidence (and Skuld's rules) decide acceptance or escalation to a bigger node — the cost shape that makes small models mighty.
slices.title: The cascade

slices.text: Draft-and-review: a Forge-role node drafts, an Auditor-role node reviews against invariants, a revision loop bounded by policy.
slices.title: Draft-and-review

slices.text: Decompose-and-delegate: a planner splits a task into sub-tasks dealt across worlds (the Mythic crew pattern as mesh behaviour), gathering with the Y-083 lifecycle.
slices.title: Decompose-and-delegate

slices.text: Ensemble cost accounting: every pattern reports its true cost (node-seconds, energy estimate) against single-model baselines.

slices.text: Deterministic tier (Hermes contract): tasks marked deterministic are answered without models at all where a registered deterministic handler exists — the mesh respects the cheapest truth.

slices.text: Níðhöggr: abuse prevention at scale — threat catalogue and countermeasure prototypes (rate, reputation, attestation).
